record.paper_title: Complete intersection liaison and Gorenstein liaison: new results and open problems
record.original_question: Let C_t be an arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay curve in P^n whose homogeneous ideal I(C_t) has the t-linear free resolution 0 -> R(-t-2)^((t^2+t)/2) -> R(-t-1)^(t^2+2t) -> R(-t)^((t^2+3t+2)/2) -> I(C_t) -> 0 over the homogeneous coordinate ring R. Is every such curve C_t glicci, meaning in the Gorenstein liaison class of a complete intersection?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$ and $t\ge 1$ be integers, and let $R=k[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ denote the homogeneous coordinate ring of projective space $\mathbb{P}^n$ over a field $k$. Suppose $C_t\subset\mathbb{P}^n$ is an arithmetically Cohen–Macaulay (ACM) curve whose homogeneous ideal $I(C_t)\subset R$ admits the $t$-linear minimal free resolution
$$0\longrightarrow R(-t-2)^{\binom{t+1}{2}}\longrightarrow R(-t-1)^{t^2+2t}\longrightarrow R(-t)^{\binom{t+2}{2}}\longrightarrow I(C_t)\longrightarrow 0.$$
Recall that a subscheme is called glicci if it belongs to the Gorenstein liaison class of a complete intersection, i.e., it can be linked to a complete intersection by a finite sequence of arithmetically Gorenstein links.

Question: Is every such curve $C_t$ glicci?
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of whether every ACM subscheme of $\mathbb{P}^n$ is glicci is a well-known open problem in liaison theory. For codimension-2 ACM subschemes the answer is affirmative, and Migliore–Nagel showed that any ACM subscheme becomes glicci after re-embedding into $\mathbb{P}^{n+1}$. The specific case of curves with a $t$-linear resolution in arbitrary $\mathbb{P}^n$ does not appear to have been settled in the searched literature, so the status is taken as unknown.

status_evidence.title: GLICCI IDEALS (Migliore–Nagel)
status_evidence.snippet: A central problem is to decide whether every ACM subscheme of projective n-space is glicci.
status_evidence.claim: Whether every ACM subscheme is glicci is a central open problem.

status_evidence.title: Monomial Ideals and the Gorenstein Liaison Class of a Complete Intersection
status_evidence.snippet: Any reduced ACM subscheme of P^n becomes glicci when viewed as a subscheme of P^{n+1}.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist via re-embedding, but the original-space question remains.

status_evidence.title: Gorenstein Liaison and ACM Sheaves
status_evidence.snippet: All codimension 2 ACM schemes are glicci.
status_evidence.claim: Codimension 2 case is settled; higher codimension cases (including curves in P^n for n>=4) remain generally open.
